etymology_text: Inherited from Old East Slavic двьрь (dvĭrĭ), from Proto-Slavic *dvьrь, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *dwírs, from Proto-Indo-European *dʰwṓr, whence English door, Lithuanian durys, Latin forum, Sanskrit द्वार (dvā́ra).

etymology_templates.name: inh+
etymology_templates.expansion: Inherited from Old East Slavic двьрь (dvĭrĭ)

examples.text: — За дверьми́? За дверя́ми лежа́ла? За дверя́ми? — вскрича́л вдруг Раско́льников, му́тным, испу́ганным взгля́дом смотря́ на Разуми́хина, и ме́дленно приподня́лся, опира́ясь руко́й, на дива́не.
examples.ref: 1866, Фёдор Достоевский [Fyodor Dostoevsky], “Часть II, Глава IV”, in Преступление и наказание; English translation from Constance Garnett, transl., Crime and Punishment, 1914:
examples.english: "Behind the door? Lying behind the door? Behind the door?" Raskolnikov cried suddenly, staring with a blank look of terror at Razumihin, and he slowly sat up on the sofa, leaning on his hand.
examples.roman: — Za dverʹmí? Za dverjámi ležála? Za dverjámi? — vskričál vdrug Raskólʹnikov, mútnym, ispúgannym vzgljádom smotrjá na Razumíxina, i médlenno pripodnjálsja, opirájasʹ rukój, na diváne.
examples.translation: "Behind the door? Lying behind the door? Behind the door?" Raskolnikov cried suddenly, staring with a blank look of terror at Razumihin, and he slowly sat up on the sofa, leaning on his hand.

examples.text: Дверь то́тчас же откры́лась. За две́рью стоя́л босо́й мальчи́шка, краси́вый, сму́глый, с о́чень я́ркими губа́ми.
examples.ref: 1907, Фёдор Сологуб [Fyodor Sologub], chapter II, in Маленький человек; English translation from Paul Selver, transl., The Tiny Man, 1919:
examples.english: The door opened immediately. Behind the door stood a bare-footed lad, well-favoured, brown-skinned, with very full-coloured lips.
examples.roman: Dverʹ tótčas že otkrýlasʹ. Za dvérʹju stojál bosój malʹčíška, krasívyj, smúglyj, s óčenʹ járkimi gubámi.
examples.translation: The door opened immediately. Behind the door stood a bare-footed lad, well-favoured, brown-skinned, with very full-coloured lips.

 *bʰréh₂tēr

Cognates include Sanskrit भ्रातृ (bhrātṛ), Latin frāter, English brother and English pal.
